sections.title: Stance and focus adverbs
sections.content: Most adverbs tell you how something happens: *Habló lentamente*. A stance adverb steps outside the action and comments on the whole sentence: how frank, sure or glad the speaker is. *Francamente, no me convence la propuesta* means 'I will be frank: the proposal does not convince me', not 'it does not convince me frankly'. A focus adverb such as *precisamente*, which you met in the last lesson, points at the word after it and means 'exactly that'.

sections.title: Common stance and focus adverbs
rows: frankly, honestly: you are direct about your opinion
fortunately, unfortunately: your feeling about a fact
actually, in fact: you correct what someone expected or assumed
strictly speaking: you give the exact, technical truth
strictly so-called, in the true sense: it follows the noun
precisely, exactly: it points at the word after it
barely, only just: it limits an amount

sections.title: Where they go, and the commas
sections.content: A stance adverb can open the sentence, sit in the middle or close it, and a comma marks each edge: *Lamentablemente, no hay presupuesto.* / *El proyecto, lamentablemente, no tiene presupuesto.* / *No hay presupuesto, lamentablemente.* Right after the verb with no commas, the same word usually describes how something was done: *Ana me habló sinceramente* means 'Ana spoke to me honestly'. *Rotundamente*, *notablemente* and *deliberadamente* usually describe the action: *Rechazó rotundamente la acusación*. *Precisamente* and *apenas* take no commas, because they sit right in front of the word they point at.

items.spanish: Francamente, no me convence la propuesta.
items.english: Frankly, the proposal does not convince me.

items.spanish: El proyecto, lamentablemente, no tiene presupuesto este año.
items.english: The project, unfortunately, has no budget this year.

items.spanish: En realidad, no fue un error, sino una decisión.
items.english: Actually, it was not a mistake but a decision.

items.spanish: En rigor, la fecha límite venció ayer.
items.english: Strictly speaking, the deadline expired yesterday.

items.spanish: No es una ciudad propiamente dicha, sino un pueblo grande.
items.english: It is not a city in the true sense, but a big town.

items.spanish: El ministro rechazó rotundamente la acusación.
items.english: The minister flatly rejected the accusation.

sections.content: Try the comma test: if you can pause and put commas round the adverb, it is commenting on the whole sentence. Use one stance adverb per sentence; two in a row sound heavy.
